headline: QA-focused roundup: Playwright adds test locks; agentic vulnerability harnesses and package-manager changes that affect test reliability

top_signal.title: Playwright v1.63.0 — named test locks and richer traces to reduce parallel-test interference
top_signal.summary: Playwright 1.63.0 adds named test locks so tests that touch a shared resource never run concurrently, plus richer tracing (ARIA/screen snapshots) and step params for better failure triage and reporting.
top_signal.why_it_matters: Named locks let teams run tests in parallel while preventing shared-resource collisions, reducing flaky failures and simplifying CI shard design and triage.

items.title: Google open-sources Mantis — an agentic harness for finding, reproducing and fixing vulnerabilities
items.summary: Google published Mantis, an open-source harness combining agentic analysis, repository-history summarization, sandboxed reproduction and critic/review agents to reduce hallucinated findings and increase true positives in automated vulnerability discovery.
items.why_it_matters: QA teams can integrate Mantis to triage AI-discovered security findings, reproduce issues in sandboxes, and reduce false positives before test or release gates.

items.title: vlt 1.0 GA — drop-in npm replacement with phased installs and malware-blocking registries
items.summary: vlt 1.0 (by the original npm team) ships phased installs (separate download and build steps), queryable dependency-graph selectors, and hosted registries that reject known-malicious packages by default.
items.why_it_matters: Phased installs and registry malware-blocking improve reproducibility and reduce supply-chain risk in test runners and CI agents, changing how teams should validate test environment setup.

items.title: Figma documents internal use of AI agents for security alert triage and investigation
items.summary: Figma published an internal engineering write-up describing AI agents that search incidents, summarize past investigations, run checks across systems, and prepare candidate fixes to accelerate security triage.
items.why_it_matters: Shows practical agent patterns QA teams can adapt for failure triage, automated root-cause searches, and surfacing reproducible evidence for flaky or failing tests.

items.title: Kubernetes v1.37 promotes KubeletInUserNamespace (rootless kubelet) to Beta
items.summary: Kubernetes v1.37 moves KubeletInUserNamespace (rootless mode) to Beta, enabling node components (kubelet, CRI, CNI, kube-proxy) to run as non-root using Linux user namespaces.
items.why_it_matters: Running kubelet and runtimes non-root reduces blast radius for test infrastructure and CI agents, but QA teams must validate privileged assumptions in device/cluster tests and update test images and tooling.

items.title: Kubernetes v1.37 DRA updates — Device Resource API improvements affecting node scheduling and resource tests
items.summary: v1.37 advances Device Resource API (DRA) updates into Beta/Alpha stages, changing how device attributes and fractional capacities are expressed to the scheduler and kubelet.
items.why_it_matters: QA responsible for performance, device-specific, or node-resource tests must revisit testbeds and assertions: DRA changes affect resource claims, scheduling behavior, and node oversubscription assumptions.
